subject.declared_domain: NFRA_GLOBGRPH P2-STITCH step-1 -- the L1/L5 portal+pipeline extractor. Reuses the existing comp-graph substrate rather than inventing extraction (trace_graph.build_graph + cache_cli's React Query key extractor), normalizes the comp-trace vocabulary to the FROZEN comp-aws/NFRA_COMPAWS schema, and emits the portal/pipeline-OWNED node classes plus the INTRA-layer edges in comp_aws_cli graph-dict shape. The cross-layer STITCH edges to the AWS layer are deliberately NOT its job -- those are step-2, derive_stitch.py, subject 1 on this face.

as_of.graph_vintage: Holds no stored vintage: it rebuilds its subgraph from the working tree on every call (trace_graph.build_graph(ws) plus a scan of portal/src). Its output's freshness is therefore the WORKING TREE's, not a pinned artifact's -- a property with no timestamp anywhere in the emitted meta.

methodology.how: build_portal_stitch_graph(ws) calls trace_graph.build_graph(ws), then emits nodes in two passes: trace nodes whose node_type is in NODE_TYPE_MAP (COMPONENT/ENDPOINT/S3_ARTIFACT/GOLD_SCRIPT -> the four PRD classes), and REACT_QUERY_KEY nodes from cache_cli, plus one synthetic PORTAL_BUNDLE root. emit() dedups on node_id via a `seen` set. Two joins are then attempted per query key -- component -[QUERIES]-> key, and key -[FETCHES]-> api_route -- each by _match_component / _match_endpoint. Finally the trace edges whose type is in EDGE_TYPE_MAP are kept ONLY when BOTH endpoints were emitted, giving 0-dangling within the subgraph by construction; edges are deduped on (source, target, edge_type).

stages_inferential: _match_component (:171-176): matches a cache_cli component STEM against emitted PORTAL_COMPONENT nodes by THREE alternative predicates -- id.endswith('#'+stem) OR name == stem OR id.endswith(stem) -- and returns the FIRST hit. The third predicate is a bare suffix match, so two components whose ids both end with the stem resolve to whichever was emitted first, with nothing recorded.
_match_endpoint (:178-182): same shape, name == fn OR id.endswith(fn), first hit wins. A wrong match here produces a QUERIES/FETCHES edge that is structurally valid and semantically wrong.

the component-identity mismatch these two exist to bridge is declared in the source: trace_graph ids components as 'file#Component' while cache_cli yields the bare stem, so the join is a suffix heuristic rather than a shared key
stages_deterministic: the NODE_TYPE_MAP / EDGE_TYPE_MAP vocabulary normalisation -- closed dicts, an unmapped type is skipped rather than guessed (:120-127, :131-136)
the both-endpoints-emitted edge filter, which makes intra-subgraph 0-dangling structural rather than checked (:144-150)
node dedup on the `seen` set and edge dedup on (source, target, edge_type)

coverage.universe: Every trace_graph node whose node_type is one of the four in NODE_TYPE_MAP, every React Query key cache_cli can parse out of portal/src, one synthetic root, and every trace edge whose type is in EDGE_TYPE_MAP and whose BOTH endpoints were emitted.
coverage.denominator: ⛔ ABSENT WHERE IT MATTERS MOST, AND IT IS ABSENT BY DISCARD RATHER THAN BY OMISSION. cache_cli.extract returns a THREE-tuple -- (entries, unparseable, total) -- and the shim at :67 destructures it as `entries, _unparseable, _total` and RETURNS ONLY entries. The upstream tool computes exactly the denominator a consumer needs (how many keys existed, how many could not be parsed) and this adapter throws both away, so the emitted REACT_QUERY_KEY count is a numerator with no denominator anywhere downstream. _summarize prints per-class node counts and per-verb edge counts, which describe what WAS emitted and can say nothing about what was not.
explicitly_out: comp-trace LAMBDA / EVENTBRIDGE / CLOUDFRONT / UNKNOWN node types -- deliberately not re-emitted here because they are canonical in the ARN-keyed AWS layer; declared in the source and correct
cross-layer edges to LAMBDA / S3_BUCKET -- deferred to step-2 by design

trace edges whose type is not in EDGE_TYPE_MAP, and edges with an endpoint outside the emitted set -- both skipped with NO counter, so the intra-subgraph 0-dangling property is achieved partly by dropping edges silently rather than only by scope
React Query keys cache_cli could not parse -- counted by cache_cli, discarded by the shim (see denominator)
a duplicate node_id -- emit() returns early on a `seen` hit with no counter, so a genuine identity collision between two sources is indistinguishable from a single node
a query key whose component or endpoint does not match -- _match_component / _match_endpoint return None and the edge is simply not appended, with no counter

files cache_cli could not READ -- skipped at cache_cli.py:281-284 WITHOUT incrementing `total`, so they are absent from the denominator as well as the numerator; a denominator with a hole in it cannot be repaired by carrying it

The unmatched-join skips at :134-140. _summarize :186-199 prints only emitted counts. ⛔ THE CONTRAST WITHIN THIS FACE IS THE POINT: kuzu_nessie_load.py (subject 2) counts key_collisions and skipped_missing_endpoint and prints both; derive_stitch.py (subject 1) counts lam_unmatched and carries the unmatched set. key.identity_space: Node ids are inherited from trace_graph verbatim for the four mapped classes, so this module does not mint identity for them -- it re-labels their CLASS. It mints exactly two id forms of its own: the synthetic root and the React Query key ids. Edge endpoints are those same ids, and the both-endpoints-in-`seen` filter makes an edge expressible only within the emitted id space.
key.key_expression: TRACE-DERIVED NODES: key = n.id verbatim from trace_graph.build_graph(ws) (:122-125) -- unchanged, unnormalised, no fallback. SYNTHETIC ROOT: the literal string 'portal' (:114). REACT QUERY KEYS: key = 'rqk:' + ce.query_key, where ce.query_key is cache_cli's verbatim key_str (:129, shim :62). DEDUP: emit() admits a node only if key not in `seen` (:104-106), first writer wins. EDGE KEY: the 3-tuple (source, target, edge_type) (:152-155), last writer wins -- note this is the OPPOSITE precedence to the node dedup in the same function, and neither is recorded on the output.
key.declared_mapping: The class vocabulary mapping is declared twice -- as a table in the module docstring (:19-27) and as the NODE_TYPE_MAP / EDGE_TYPE_MAP dicts (:71-84) -- and the two agree. What is NOT declared is the JOIN: that a QUERIES or FETCHES edge is produced by suffix matching between two different id conventions, and that the first match wins. The docstring presents '(+ REACT_QUERY_KEY from cache_cli)' and '(cache) -> QUERIES' as if the join were given rather than inferred.
key.evidence: Node id passthrough :125; synthetic root :114; rqk id :129; shim key_str mapping :62; emit dedup :104-106; edge dedup :152-155; the two matchers :171-182. Rated UNSTABLE because the module joins TWO id conventions with a suffix heuristic: trace_graph's 'file#Component' against cache_cli's bare stem, resolved by id.endswith(stem) among others. A stem that is a suffix of more than one component id has no defined winner beyond emission order, and emission order is trace_graph's dict order -- so the same input can in principle yield a different join without any input changing.

failure_mode.returns_on_failure: NO LOCAL EXCEPTION CONVERSION, BUT NOT FAIL-LOUD -- and the distinction is the whole point of this row. A handler census of this module finds ZERO except-handlers in its 224 lines, so it never converts an exception into a value ITSELF. ⛔ THAT IS A LOCAL FACT AND IT DOES NOT MAKE THE PATH FAIL LOUDLY, because the collapse already happened one module upstream. cache_cli.extract() at org/modules/graph/cache_cli.py:268-289 @5da9e7fffc: ':278-279' returns (entries=[], unparseable=[], total=0) when portal_src DOES NOT EXIST -- a silent empty, not a raise; and ':281-284' wraps the per-file read in 'try: ... except Exception: continue', so an unreadable file is SKIPPED. This module consumes that already-collapsed three-tuple through its shim and cannot distinguish 'portal/src is absent' from 'portal/src has no query keys'. ⛔ AND THE NORMAL RUN DOES NOT ASSERT ANYTHING: the empty-class and 0-dangling assertions live behind --selftest (:212-217); a default CLI run calls _summarize and returns 0, and the in-process derive_stitch path never reaches main() at all. So a missing portal/src yields a structurally valid graph with zero REACT_QUERY_KEY nodes, no error, and rc=0. WHAT REMAINS TRUE AND IS STILL WORTH CREDITING, SPLIT BY AXIS BECAUSE THE TWO AXES HAVE OPPOSITE ANSWERS. ON THE EXCEPTION AXIS the credit holds: this module adds no handler of its own, so it never converts an exception into a value, never invents a fallback and never asserts a cause -- a trace_graph failure or an unimportable cache_cli DOES propagate through it, and the exception-path collapse it is subject to (absent dir, unreadable file) is INHERITED from cache_cli. ⛔ ON THE DATA AXIS THE CREDIT DOES NOT HOLD AND THIS CARD PROVES IT: the silent losses are MANUFACTURED HERE, by ordinary control flow rather than by exception handling -- the shim's discard of `unparseable` and `total` (:67) is a LOCAL choice, and so are the uncounted drops at emit()'s `seen` guard (:104-106), the unmapped-type skips (:123-124, :146-147), the unmatched-join skips (:134-140) and the both-endpoints edge filter (:148-149). None of those is an except-handler and every one of them loses data with no counter. So: EXCEPTION-path degradation inherited, DATA-path degradation manufactured locally.
silent_degrade_paths: UPSTREAM, and it dominates the local reading: cache_cli.extract returns ([], [], 0) when portal_src does not exist (cache_cli.py:278-279). A missing or renamed portal/src therefore produces zero REACT_QUERY_KEY nodes, no error and rc=0 -- identical output to a portal with no useQuery call sites

UPSTREAM: per-file read exceptions are caught and skipped (cache_cli.py:281-284, 'except Exception: continue'), and `total` is NOT incremented for a skipped file -- so an unreadable file is absent from the numerator AND from the denominator. Even a shim that KEPT the denominator could not see this class

the shim (:67) discards cache_cli's `unparseable` and `total`, so a portal/src change that makes half the query keys unparseable produces a smaller REACT_QUERY_KEY set. The COUNT does change and _summarize prints it, so this is not invisible -- what is missing is anything that marks the smaller number as a SHORTFALL: with the denominator discarded, 'the portal genuinely has fewer query keys' and 'half of them stopped parsing' render as the same integer. The upstream computed the discriminator (and even renders it, cache_cli._denominator_line :292-295) and the adapter dropped it

cache_cli's own DECLARED coverage limit -- 'useQueries / useInfiniteQuery / useAutoSaveQuery are NOT audited by this tool' (:294-295) -- is carried in the denominator line the shim discards, so that limit never reaches any consumer of this module's output either
the assertions that would catch an empty extraction run ONLY under --selftest (:212-217); the default CLI path and the in-process derive_stitch path both skip them

_match_component / _match_endpoint returning None (:174-176, :181-182) skips the QUERIES / FETCHES edge with no counter, so 'this component has no query key' and 'the suffix heuristic failed' are the same observable
a FIRST-hit suffix match that is WRONG (:174, id.endswith(stem)) produces a structurally valid edge to the wrong node
emit()'s `seen` early return (:104-106) drops a duplicate node_id with no counter, unlike kuzu_nessie_load which counts key_collisions for the same situation

the both-endpoints filter (:148-149) drops an edge whose endpoint was not emitted, with no counter -- so the advertised intra-subgraph 0-dangling property is partly achieved BY the silent dropping rather than only by scoping

verdict.why: The design is disciplined in the ways this face keeps rewarding: it reuses the existing comp-graph substrate instead of inventing extraction, normalises to a FROZEN schema through closed dicts so an unmapped type is skipped rather than guessed, makes intra-subgraph 0-dangling structural via a both-endpoints filter, declares its class vocabulary twice in agreeing forms, and adds NO exception handler of its own -- so on the EXCEPTION axis it never manufactures a fallback or asserts a cause, and the collapse it suffers there is inherited from cache_cli rather than invented here. QUALIFIED on three measured defects. FIRST AND WORST: the shim at :67 destructures cache_cli's (entries, unparseable, total) and keeps only entries. Its own upstream computes -- and even renders, at cache_cli._denominator_line :292-295 -- the exact denominator a consumer needs, and this adapter discards it, so the emitted REACT_QUERY_KEY population is a numerator that cannot be checked. The contrast is internal to this face: kuzu_nessie_load counts key_collisions and skipped_missing_endpoint, derive_stitch counts and carries lam_unmatched; this is the only subject that was HANDED its denominator and threw it away. SECOND: the QUERIES and FETCHES edges rest on first-hit suffix matching across two id conventions, and a wrong match is structurally valid and unmarked while the docstring presents the join as given. THIRD, and it corrects a credit I wrongly gave this subject in the first version of this card: having zero local exception handlers does NOT make this path fail loudly. cache_cli.extract returns an empty three-tuple for an ABSENT portal/src (:278-279) and skips unreadable files (:281-284) without incrementing total, so the collapse happens one module upstream and arrives here already-collapsed; and the assertions that would catch an empty extraction run only under --selftest, while the default CLI path and the in-process derive_stitch path skip them. A missing portal/src therefore yields a structurally valid graph with zero query keys, no error and rc=0. What survives as a genuine credit is narrower than I first wrote and must be SPLIT BY AXIS, because this card documents both answers: on the EXCEPTION axis the module adds no collapse of its own and inherits cache_cli's, unlike subjects 3 and 4 which manufacture theirs; on the DATA axis it manufactures its own silent loss locally -- the shim's discard and four uncounted drops, none of them an except-handler. None of the three defects needs redesign; the first is a two-line change to carry two integers the upstream already returns.
blocking_defects: the cache_cli shim (:67) discards `unparseable` and `total`, destroying a denominator its own upstream computes and renders (cache_cli._denominator_line :292-295) -- the REACT_QUERY_KEY count is unauditable downstream and a parse regression in portal/src would not be marked as a shortfall (coverage row)

the fail-loud property does NOT hold transitively: cache_cli.extract returns an empty three-tuple for an absent portal/src (:278-279) and skips unreadable files (:281-284) without counting them, so a missing portal/src yields a valid graph with zero query keys and rc=0. The empty-class assertions run only under --selftest (:212-217), which neither the default CLI path nor the in-process derive_stitch path takes (failure_mode row)

QUERIES / FETCHES edges are produced by first-hit suffix matching across two id conventions (_match_component :171-176, _match_endpoint :178-182); a wrong match is structurally valid and unmarked, and the docstring presents the join as given rather than inferred (key + methodology.invents rows)

every drop in this module is uncounted -- unmatched joins, unmapped types, duplicate ids, and endpoint-filtered edges -- so the output can be smaller than the truth with nothing marking it as a shortfall. The emitted totals ARE printed by _summarize; what no instrument carries is the denominator those totals should be read against (coverage + failure_mode rows)
